summary: Bundled skills invoke external network utilities but no installer-side exfiltration observed
details: opencode-skills-collection ships a large collection of skill bundles under bundled-skills/. Several of these contain scripts that make outbound network calls: rclone-cli/scripts/install.sh runs `curl https://rclone.org` to fetch rclone from its official project domain; youtube-notetaker/scripts/verify.sh performs curl-based GET checks; junta-leiloeiros ships Python scrapers using ping/GET/POST primitives; loki-mode/benchmarks/run-benchmarks.sh contains curl usage in benchmark tooling. These scripts are content of skill bundles, not npm lifecycle hooks, and are invoked only when the user explicitly runs the corresponding skill. Destinations that are named (rclone.org) match the tool being fetched. No install-time or import-time execution of remote content is present in package.json, no hardcoded attacker C2, no installer-secret reads (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, browser profiles), no environment scraping, and no obfuscation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
